key_terms: A set of Ballista tasks that can run under the same dependency boundary. A downstream stage starts only after the shuffle output it reads is available.
One unit of work that a scheduler assigns to an executor, usually one partition of one stage. It is neither an Arrow record batch nor necessarily a whole stage.
The exchange that writes or exposes intermediate partitions by grouping key so downstream tasks can read their required inputs.
A per-partition result, such as a sum by region, computed before the shuffle and combined into the final aggregate afterward.
An uneven key distribution that makes one task or partition much larger than the others, so it dominates the stage's completion time.

worked_examples.title: Capture plan text and hot-key results
worked_examples.code:
cd work/ballista
bash run.sh plans
bash run.sh evidence
worked_examples.interpretation: The plans receipt holds the EXPLAIN text for the regional aggregate and a hot_key_rows list for a 200-row source where 180 rows share the key hot. That list should show hot with n of 180 and twenty rare keys with n of 1, matching the fixture oracle. Look in the plan text for a repartition between partial and final aggregation; that boundary is where a hot key concentrates on one task.

worked_examples.title: Compute the hot-key oracle independently
worked_examples.code:
from collections import Counter

hot = [{"id": i, "region": "hot" if i < 180 else f"rare-{i}", "amount": 1} for i in range(200)]
counts = Counter(row["region"] for row in hot)
print(counts.most_common(2), len(counts))
worked_examples.interpretation: One region holds 180 of 200 rows and the other 20 appear once each, giving 21 groups. That distribution is what makes the final aggregate stage uneven: whichever task receives hot does most of the stage work. The engine result must equal this oracle, but equality proves only correctness; a local frequency count says nothing about task timing, which needs scheduler telemetry.

evidence: Project-only actual product commands with independent fixture oracles. Source preparation, native runtime observations and restart evidence are recorded separately in the workshop qualification ledger.
